channel.title: COI Journal
channel.description: Construction insurance compliance, reported. Published by Forsured.

item.title: Why we're starting COI Journal
item.description: COI Journal is a new publication on construction insurance compliance, published by Forsured. What we'll cover, what we won't, and how we'll earn your trust.

item.title: A certificate is not coverage: six ways contractor COIs fail project requirements
item.description: A COI Journal white paper on why contractor certificates of insurance pass a glance and still fail the project, and the six failure modes worth checking.

item.title: Rented, falsified, excluded: what 2026's cases say about trusting a contractor COI
item.description: A COI Journal analyst brief on four 2026 fraud and coverage cases, what a certificate could and couldn't have shown in each, and the checks that matter.

item.title: Why every trade sends a certificate: the COI's job in construction risk transfer
item.description: A COI Journal white paper on what a certificate of insurance is, why general contractors collect one from every trade, and what it can and can't prove.

item.title: How to read a COI against contract requirements, line by line
item.description: A COI Journal white paper: a box-by-box method for reading an ACORD 25 certificate against a project's insurance requirements, with what each box can't show.

item.title: Additional insured endorsements, explained: CG 20 10, CG 20 37 and the automatic forms
item.description: A COI Journal white paper on additional insured endorsements: what CG 20 10, CG 20 37, CG 20 38 and the automatic forms do, and how to check them.

item.title: When a contractor's coverage lapses mid-project: the exposure and the playbook
item.description: A COI Journal white paper on what a GC is exposed to when a trade's insurance lapses or is cancelled mid-project, and a step-by-step playbook to respond.

item.title: What goes into subcontract insurance requirements: a field guide for GCs and brokers
item.description: A COI Journal white paper on the insurance requirements GCs put in subcontracts, piece by piece, with real examples from two public owners' published exhibits.

item.title: The broker's side of the COI: why requests pile up and how to answer deficiency notices
item.description: A COI Journal white paper for construction brokers on where COI and endorsement requests come from, why deficiency notices repeat, and a way to cut the load.

item.title: Spreadsheet, service or software: a vendor-neutral way to choose how to manage contractor COIs
item.description: A COI Journal white paper comparing spreadsheets, outsourced tracking services and software for contractor COIs, with a scoring method that names no vendors.

item.title: Can AI review a COI? What machines do well, and where people stay in the loop
item.description: A COI Journal white paper on what AI can and can't do when reviewing contractor COIs and endorsements against project requirements, and where people stay in charge.

item.title: One set of rules per project: tracking requirements and renewals across active jobs
item.description: A COI Journal white paper on running different insurance requirements per project and keeping every contractor renewal current across a portfolio of jobs.

item.title: Closing a coverage gap without the email chain: a deficiency workflow for GCs and brokers
item.description: A COI Journal white paper on a deficiency workflow that helps GCs, trades and brokers close contractor coverage gaps in one pass instead of an email chain.

item.title: What to require from any COI tool: a vendor-neutral specification
item.description: A COI Journal white paper with a vendor-neutral specification for COI tracking tools: what to require, how to test it, and the questions to ask in a demo.

item.title: The ACORD 25's new limits sentence: what changed in the 2025/12 edition, and what GCs should do
item.description: A COI Journal analyst brief on the ACORD 25 (2025/12) limits wording: certificates may now show requested limits rather than full policy limits.

item.title: The Q3 2026 insurance market for contractors: casualty up, property down, and what it means for endorsements
item.description: A COI Journal analyst brief on Q3 2026 commercial insurance rates from Marsh's index, construction carrier growth, and what it means for contractor requirements.

item.title: What insurance regulators say about AI, and what it means for AI-assisted COI review
item.description: A COI Journal analyst brief on the NAIC's AI model bulletin, its adoption by 24 states and D.C., the 2026 pilot, and lessons for buyers of AI-assisted COI review.

item.title: Checking workers' comp yourself: what public proof of coverage lookups can and can't tell you
item.description: A COI Journal analyst brief on public workers' comp proof of coverage lookups in New York, Florida and elsewhere, what they show, and their limits for GCs.

item.title: Underreported payroll: what six construction workers' comp fraud cases show GCs
item.description: A COI Journal analyst brief on six construction workers' comp premium fraud cases from 2022 to 2026, the common pattern, and what a GC can check.

item.title: How the ISO additional insured endorsements changed: 2004, 2013 and 2019
item.description: A COI Journal analyst brief on how ISO's additional insured endorsements changed in 2004, 2013 and 2019, and why the edition date on an endorsement matters.

item.title: Two public owners, two insurance exhibits: Oregon DOT and Sonoma County compared
item.description: A COI Journal analyst brief comparing the published contractor insurance requirements of Oregon DOT and Sonoma County, line by line, with what GCs should take away.

item.title: Wrap-ups and certificates: what changes for contractor COIs on an OCIP or CCIP
item.description: A COI Journal analyst brief on owner and contractor controlled insurance programs, what they cover and exclude, and which COIs a GC still has to collect.

item.title: Fake certificates and phantom insurers: what state regulators have warned
item.description: A COI Journal analyst brief on what New Jersey, Maryland, Texas and Florida regulators have said about false certificates, fake insurers and how to verify coverage.

item.title: What does manual COI tracking cost? Reading the one published estimate
item.description: A COI Journal analyst brief on the BCS estimate that manual COI tracking costs $36,400 a year: how it's built, what it leaves out, and how to build your own.
